annotations.text: The complete Hack-shaped boundary: instruction ROM, CPU, and data memory are connected as one inspectable computer.
A composed Hack CPU: instruction fields drive the ALU, registers, write enables, jump logic, and program counter.
The raw instruction fields plus the complementary A-instruction signal used by control paths.
The instruction bit positions are surfaced as named control signals for the CPU.
NOT is NAND with the same signal connected to both inputs.
The primitive used as the construction starting point for the Nand2Tetris hardware track.
The comp field becomes the six control signals consumed by the ALU.
Destination bits become safe register and memory enables; A-instructions always load A.
OR follows from De Morgan: NOT(NOT A NAND NOT B).
AND = NOT(NAND).
Jump bits select one of the eight Hack conditions; A-instructions are forced not to jump.
An 8-way multiplexer composed from two 4-way multiplexers and one final selector.
A two-level selection tree; SEL 0 chooses inside each pair and SEL 1 chooses the pair.
SEL=0 routes A; SEL=1 routes B.
An A-instruction carries a 15-bit literal; the generator widens it to a 16-bit data word and exposes the opcode test.
A sixteen-lane MUX with one shared selection signal.
The A register stores addresses and A-instruction values.
Sixteen BIT cells in parallel form the 16-bit register.
A one-bit state cell: LOAD selects new input data; otherwise the DFF feeds its own stored value back.
The D register stores general-purpose computation results.
Hack-style ALU control: zero/negate each operand, choose AND or ADD, then optionally negate the result.
Sixteen one-bit NOT chips share the same construction pattern.
Sixteen one-bit AND chips operate in parallel.
A ripple-carry 16-bit adder. The least-significant full adder receives CIN.
Two half adders plus OR combine the carry paths.
SUM is XOR; CARRY is AND.
XOR = (A OR B) AND NOT(A AND B), expressed using the NAND-derived parts.
An 8-input OR tree built from the one-bit OR chip.
The program counter is a counter with a reset path; RESET selects zero before LOAD and INC.
A register that holds its value, loads a word, or increments it on the next clock.
The named 16-bit register landmark, composed from sixteen one-bit BIT cells.
Increment is addition by one, with a 16-bit zero as the second operand.
The instruction-memory boundary: the program counter addresses a read-only 16-bit word.
Read-only 32K x 16-bit instruction storage.
The explicit data/control boundary between CPU and memory devices.
A composed memory map: the decoder enables RAM, screen, or keyboard data and the selected device is returned to the CPU.
Hack address ranges: bit 14 selects the upper device space, bit 13 separates screen from keyboard, and lower bits identify the keyboard address.
RAM4K banks selected by the upper address bits.
A memory-mapped 16-bit screen surface. The engine owns the pixel storage contract.
The keyboard boundary exposes a 16-bit key code to the computer.
Sixteen one-bit OR chips operate in parallel.
